title: Design System: DJ Pablito Dyr Producciones

display.purpose: Hero headline only. Uppercase, poster scale, breaks across lines instead of shrinking.

headline.purpose: Section titles via SectionHeading. Uppercase at 4xl to 7xl across breakpoints.

title.purpose: Plan names, hour counts, and prices inside plan rows.

body.purpose: Descriptions and copy. Cream for primary, warm gray for secondary.

label.purpose: Kickers, buttons, chips, legends, badges, and the reservation line.

narrative.overview:
The system is a dark room with one warm light in it. Every surface is a warm near-black — never a neutral gray — and the only saturated color available is a single amber family borrowed from stage lighting. Nothing glows without purpose: the amber sits on prices, on primary actions, on kickers, and on the thin line under the active nav item, and it stays scarce everywhere else. The result reads as a booth at night, not as a nightclub flyer.

Type does the shouting so the layout does not have to. Bebas Neue condensed uppercase carries every heading, plan name, and price at poster scale, while Montserrat — in small, tight, mostly gray-cream body sizes — handles everything that has to be read rather than scanned. Sections are separated by a single hairline rule instead of large gaps, which keeps the page dense and continuous, the way a set runs without a break.

The world is content-led and mobile-first. Video loops of real parties and the booth itself are the primary imagery and they are the only elements allowed a deep shadow; interface surfaces stay flat with a hairline border. Numbers are treated as content: prices render in display type at the same weight as headings, because a customer who already knows the price before calling is the whole point of this site.
keyCharacteristics: Warm black ground (#0c0a09) with warm brown-black surfaces, never gray.
One accent hue only: amber gold, used on ≤10% of any screen.
Poster-case display type for headings, plan names, and prices.
Hairline section rules instead of whitespace-only separation.
Flat interface surfaces; depth reserved for photography and video.
Mobile-first density with 44px minimum touch targets.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue. No second saturated color enters the system — not for success, not for a badge, not for a social platform's brand color. src/test/design-tokens.test.ts enforces this against Tailwind's default palettes; treat that test as the rule's implementation.

rules.name: The No Neutral Gray Rule
rules.body: Every dark value is warm. #000, #fff, slate, zinc, and cool grays are banned. If a surface needs to be darker or lighter, mix the warm ink toward the warm paper, not toward gray.

rules.name: The Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Amber is the price of attention and the budget is small. If two elements compete for the accent on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Poster Case Rule
rules.body: Display type is always uppercase; body type is never uppercase. There is no third case rule and no sentence-case heading.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Content Rule
rules.body: A price renders in Bebas Neue at heading scale with the accent color. Prices never get demoted to a gray label — the published price is the argument.

rules.name: The Two Families Rule
rules.body: Adding a third family is a system change, not a detail. If Montserrat cannot carry a role, the answer is weights and tracking, not a new font.

rules.name: The Lit Media Rule
rules.body: Only media lifts. A button, panel, fieldset, or card gets a border and a surface step; if it needs a shadow to be seen, the fill or the border is wrong.

rules.name: The Warm Light Rule
rules.body: Depth gradients are amber at 7–16% opacity, falling away to transparent. A gray or black gradient fill is a different system.

dos: Do keep every dark value warm; pull new neutrals by mixing toward #f4ede4 and #0c0a09, never toward gray.
Do set prices, plan names, and section titles in Bebas Neue uppercase at heading scale.
Do separate sections with border-t border-line and keep vertical rhythm at py-12 md:py-20.
Do give every control a 44px minimum touch target and a visible amber focus ring.
Do write Spanish-first UI copy and keep Spanish plan names on one line via display type rather than shrinking the size.
Do reuse the kicker-plus-hairline SectionHeading for every new section.
Do use the amber wash gradients for depth instead of shadows on interface surfaces.
Do put text-balance on short leads and captions so they never leave a one-word last line.
Do label nav items with the name of the section they land on.
Do fade in an element that appears after a state change (120ms, pack-fade, opacity only). details cannot animate height without measuring, so a fade is the whole budget.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, including for semantic states, badges, or third-party brand colors.
Don't use pure black, pure white, slate, zinc, or cool grays — the design-tokens test enforces this and will fail the build.
Don't put shadows on buttons, cards, fieldsets, or nav.
Don't use radii above 8px on containers or rounded-full on buttons.
Don't set body copy in uppercase, or display copy in sentence case. A full sentence in uppercase at 11px — a caption, a footnote, a helper line — is body copy, not a label.
Don't lower the price to a secondary gray label or hide it behind a cotizar CTA — published price is the positioning.
Don't use clickable divs; interactive patterns are real links, real buttons, or real radio inputs inside a label.

Don't invent muted variants of paper (paper-muted, surface-muted, and the like). They are not defined in tailwind.config.mjs, so the class silently does nothing and the element inherits its parent color. Soften primary body copy with text-paper/80; use muted for helper, metadata, and secondary-value text. src/test/design-tokens.test.ts rejects both names.
